reviewerSelfCorrection.occasion: Three of the four findings this fold lands are Codex's. One of them, PLJ-V8-SF1, is a defect I had every piece of evidence for on v8 and did not charge.
reviewerSelfCorrection.whatIMissed: Frozen v8 gave OBL-ACTOR-JOIN a two-limb rideStanding but filed it in summary.deferredOrRidesElsewhere alone, so the summary named the DR-114 riding limb and concealed the G32 execution limb.
reviewerSelfCorrection.whyItSurvivedMyPass: My bucket test is mechanical: every obligation in exactly one list, no phantom, no omission, and leftoverDesign-true obligations in the leftoverDesign bucket. v8 passed all of that. The test has no notion of whether the bucket an obligation sits in actually describes its standing, and a two-limb obligation can satisfy every mechanical invariant while being filed under the limb that matters less.
reviewerSelfCorrection.compoundingFactor: This is the sharp part. My v8 verdict praised precisely the thing whose summary representation was wrong: I wrote that the repair was 'done with the right granularity' and described the obligation as carrying 'a two-limb routing'. I identified the two limbs in prose, in the same verdict, and never asked whether the summary showed both. Recognising the structure and not testing its representation is worse than not noticing the structure.
reviewerSelfCorrection.whatIChangedThisTime: Added a semantic bucket check: scan every obligation's rideStanding for a multi-limb form, and for each one require that its bucket names the limb and that a per-limb record exists. It is in attacksRun as a scan over all twenty-one obligations rather than a check on the one I already knew about.
reviewerSelfCorrection.standingLesson: A structural invariant that passes is not evidence the structure is right — only that it is well-formed. When a review notices that an object has parts, the representation of every part becomes a thing to test, not a thing to admire.
reviewerSelfCorrection.effectOnThisVerdict: None adverse to the subject. v9 corrects it, and the perLimbStanding key it adds is a stronger fix than simply re-bucketing would have been.

observationsNotFindings: The fix is better than a re-bucketing. Moving OBL-ACTOR-JOIN into qualificationAtNamedGate alone would have answered the finding literally while creating the mirror-image concealment — naming the G32 limb and hiding the DR-114 one. The added perLimbStanding key records both limbs explicitly, so neither is inferable only from a bucket choice. For an obligation that genuinely spans two rows, that is the representation the summary needed.

No obligation body changed in this fold at all. Every one of the twenty-one is byte-identical to v8, and the eight-member leftoverDesign set is identical to v7 two folds back. The measurement has been stable across v7, v8 and v9 while three summary and provenance findings were repaired around it — worth the coordinator knowing, because it means the accounting has been independently re-verified three times without moving.

The version-form finding was fixed with the generic 'Not this artifact's version number' rather than by correcting the number to v9. Every role in this file now uses that form, and the self-version scan returns zero matches of any kind. This corpus has now charged that class four times; this is the first fold in which the offending file has no concrete-version role left at all.

The file 08 pin remains correctly unchanged at f909ddff while COORD and HEAD carry post-D-170 values. D-170 was record-only, so a fold that refreshed all three governing pins would have been wrong about file 08. Two consecutive versions of this artifact have got that distinction right.

decision.summaryForCoordinator: No blockers, no should-fix. All four findings are landed and I verified each against frozen v7/v8 and the live register rather than any reviewer's account. The substantive one, PLJ-V8-SF1, was that v8 gave OBL-ACTOR-JOIN a two-limb standing but filed it in deferredOrRidesElsewhere alone, naming the DR-114 limb and concealing the G32 execution limb. v9 moves it to qualificationAtNamedGate, empties deferredOrRidesElsewhere, and adds a perLimbStanding key recording both limbs explicitly — a better fix than re-bucketing, which would have created the mirror-image concealment. The version-form finding is fixed with the immune generic form, and a self-version scan over every string field now returns zero matches of any kind. The fold is exceptionally tightly scoped: every one of the twenty-one obligation bodies is byte-identical to v8, the eight-member leftoverDesign set is identical to v7 two folds back, and only summary and provenance fields moved. All 56 basedOn pins and 57 recordedInputs recompute, and the file 08 pin is correctly left unchanged at f909ddff while COORD and HEAD carry post-D-170 values — D-170 was record-only, so refreshing all three would have been wrong. One thing I owe the record: PLJ-V8-SF1 is Codex's and I missed it on v8, despite my own v8 verdict describing the obligation as carrying 'a two-limb routing' and praising its granularity. My bucket test checks that coverage is well-formed, not that a bucket describes the standing it holds — so a two-limb obligation can pass every mechanical invariant while being filed under the limb that matters less. I added a semantic bucket check over all twenty-one obligations for this review. 19 attacks run, 19 refuted.
